assumptions: The founder uses no Reckitt confidential data, relationships, specifications, or other employer resources.
Mid-market customers lacking modern PLM can authorize supplier evidence collection and retain the service annually.
Regulatory specialists can review interpretations without eliminating attractive subscription margins.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid readiness audits converting into annual subscriptions, evidence of supplier response rates, measured onboarding and support cost per SKU, renewal intent, and validated willingness to pay among firms without capable PLM.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Making a permissioned SKU-to-proof record part of packaging approval targets a specific compliance workflow rather than offering generic document storage.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Missing packaging evidence can cause delay, redesign, and compliance expense, but mid-market budgets and urgency by SKU remain unverified.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid audits can fund onboarding into high-margin annual subscriptions, although supplier support costs, CAC, retention, and the proposed ARR scale are assumptions.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market brands and manufacturers lacking capable PLM systems form a coherent EU beachhead with meaningful recurring SKU volume.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Lightweight supplier collection and audit exports can win an underserved segment, but PLM vendors, consultants, and customer-built systems constrain dominance.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The record can extend to more packaging rules, supplier risk, claims substantiation, product compliance, and additional EU geographies.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded approval records, supplier participation, schemas, and response benchmarks could create switching costs, but none are controlled yet.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A focused evidence workflow can be materially faster and easier than spreadsheets or heavyweight PLM deployment, subject to customer validation.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: PPWR application creates a timely readiness window, although detailed obligations phase in and urgency will vary across packaging types.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Consultants, labs, and converters are credible trust-bearing channels, but no agreements, pipeline, or demonstrated CAC exists.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Document AI and data modeling fit the founder, but regulatory accuracy, supplier onboarding, security, employer separation, and specialist support add execution risk.

highest_value_structural_change: Anchor the product contractually in the packaging approval gate, with reusable supplier permissions and structured evidence records that persist across audits and SKU revisions.
main_structural_strength: The concept combines regulatory urgency with a recurring, high-margin data workflow capable of becoming embedded in customer approvals.
primary_score_limiter: The proposed dataset and workflow rights are unsigned, while PLM incumbents can bundle comparable compliance fields.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Large brands can extend existing PLM systems, and phased obligations mean many SKUs may not have enough immediate urgency to support the assumed subscription pricing.
